assessment.rationale: The supplied evidence supports a narrowly scoped engineering-gate pass, conditional on the reported artifacts and execution history being accurate. All ten reported AD/FD discrepancies are below 5% (maximum about 1.78%); the minimum signal ratio is about 14.94, maximum asymmetry about 0.275, maximum relative FD change about 0.0308, and maximum relative envelope half-width about 0.0404. These satisfy the stated thresholds without adding a noise allowance. Reported observer and fresh-process agreement checks also pass. The global-index observer repair addresses an identifiable recording defect and, as documented, is distinct from changing numerical tolerances or retrying failed derivative checks. This supports further bounded development testing—not scientific approval, exact gradient correctness, or validation of the original terminal objective.
limitations: I did not execute the experiment or independently inspect the referenced artifacts. Selected raw records support arithmetic checks, but cannot establish all artifact-validation, hash-preservation, reset, or execution-history claims.

The numerical tolerance values appear to use max(0.01, 0.05 × max(|AD|, |FD|)), not an additive '5% plus 0.01' rule. The interpretation should state the exact formula; this wording issue does not change these reported passes.

The earlier-action residual remains approximately 73.82–77.23 gradient units, or 0.449–0.469%, with AD below both observed FD envelopes. It is much larger than the observed AD repeat range and fresh-process median shift of 0.583. The fresh control therefore does not explain it, but these small empirical ranges are not confidence bounds and do not identify its cause.

Shadow kernels recompute inputs rather than capture native compiled intermediates. Zero recorded hazards establish only that none were observed in those shadow probes. There were no active particle contacts, and the supplied observer perturbations cover only the first epsilon of each instrumented case. Neither backward safety nor general contact correctness follows.

Original local-index masks are invalid and must remain excluded. The documented correction and synthetic positive controls support the recording repair, but hashes and aggregate counts alone do not establish detailed contact-identity or MILK L1 sign-change conclusions. The underlying per-frame and sign artifacts are not supplied here.

The supplied terminal excerpts support a stop-gradient/surrogate interpretation: native backward holds NumPy-derived position, ranking and scale fields constant during differentiation. Even unchanged selected identity does not make recomputed-target finite differences equivalent, because the selected position can move. The helper also runs in backward, so freezing only forward is insufficient.

Only four/eight-step partial losses were tested with max_loss_steps=1000. No terminal term, original step-999 objective, full-horizon behavior, optimizer performance, physical fidelity or paper replication has been validated.
assessment.recommended_next_test: Predeclare a bounded follow-up that retains the unresolved earlier-action residual as an explicit issue: repeat a fixed epsilon sweep with paired FD and per-loss-component diagnostics, validated global-frame contact masks, and L1 sign snapshots. Separately specify any shortened terminal diagnostic as a different objective from the original horizon. Compare native recomputed-target behavior with an explicit frozen-target diagnostic that preserves position, ranks/membership and scale through both forward and backward; record these fields for every perturbation. Establish precision and repeatability separately for each mode, without relaxing gates or automatically proceeding to optimization.

scope: Advisory interpretation and supplied-code assessment, not independent simulation or scientific approval.
